chunks: And with the first chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ja’far ibn Muhammad, from Isma’il ibn ’Abbad, from [’Abdullah ibn] Bukayr, from Abu ’Abdullah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, that he said:
Verily, we love from our Shi’ah those who are intelligent, understanding, learned in jurisprudence, forbearing, accommodating, patient, truthful, and faithful.

Then he said: Surely Allah, the Most Blessed and the Most High, has specially endowed the Prophets, peace be upon them, with the noble traits of character. So whoever has them in himself, let him praise Allah for that; and whoever does not have them, let him earnestly entreat Allah and ask Him [for them].

He [the narrator] said: I said: May I be made your ransom, what are they? He said: Piety, contentment, patience, gratitude, forbearance, modesty, generosity, courage, jealously guarding one’s honour, beneficence, truthfulness of speech, and fulfilment of trust.

key_terms.القنوع: Al-Qunu’ - Contentment: satisfaction with what Allah has provided
key_terms.الورع: Al-Wara’ - Piety/scrupulousness: careful avoidance of anything doubtful or sinful
key_terms.شيعتنا: Shi’atuna - Our followers/partisans: refers to those who follow the Ahl al-Bayt and adhere to their teachings
key_terms.صدق الحديث: Sidq al-Hadith - Truthfulness of speech: honesty and integrity in all verbal communication
key_terms.مكارم الأخلاق: Makarim al-Akhlaq - Noble character traits: the highest virtues that Allah endowed the Prophets with as exemplars for humanity

ai.seo_question: What are the twelve noble character traits (makarim al-akhlaq) that Imam al-Sadiq said Allah bestowed upon the Prophets?
ai.summary: Imam Ja’far al-Sadiq (a) describes the beloved qualities of Shi’a followers — intelligence, understanding, patience, and faithfulness — then teaches that Allah specially granted the Prophets noble character traits (makarim al-akhlaq). He enumerates twelve virtues: piety, contentment, patience, gratitude, forbearance, modesty, generosity, courage, protective honour, beneficence, truthful speech, and trustworthiness. Those who possess them should be grateful; those who lack them should earnestly beseech Allah for them.
